newsitem.title: UK: Carpetright eyes margin over sales.
newsitem.headline: Carpetright eyes margin over sales.

text.p: British carpet retailer Carpetright Plc said on Tuesday it was putting more emphasis on protecting gross margin rather than driving sales in its current year.
Chairman and chief executive Lord Harris said the group was doing a lot less discounting this year than last, which accounted in part for the lower level of sales growth.
Carpetright's comparable store sales were up four percent in the seven weeks since the start of May, but in the same period last year they were up by as much as 30 percent.
The first seven weeks of its current financial year had been a lot more profitable than last year, he told a news conference.
Harris dismissed market worries that the group's growth rate was slowing down, saying the it planned to have 450 stores by 2000, opening them at a rate of 35 a year.
This was down on last year's 65 store openings, but Harris said last year was exceptional as the group introduced its new Carpet Depot format, aimed at the higher end of market.
The group earlier reported a 28 percent increase in profits for the year to end April 1997.
